title: Skin phototherapy
what: The skin is treated with ultraviolet light in a special booth or under a lamp. A dermatologist prescribes it as a course.
why: For psoriasis, vitiligo, some types of eczema, and other skin conditions.
duration: one session lasts from a few seconds to a few minutes; a course is usually 2 to 3 times a week for several weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines. Some make you more sensitive to light
If you had skin cancer or have many moles
How you usually tan or burn in the sun

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put creams or perfume on your skin before the session, unless your doctor said otherwise.

prepare.title: Sun
prepare.text: During treatment, do not sunbathe extra or use tanning beds.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that are easy to take off.

steps: Areas that are not being treated are covered
You stand in the booth or under the lamp for the set time
The dose is slowly increased from session to session
feel: Afterward, the skin sometimes turns slightly pink
The skin may get dry. A moisturizer helps
after: Use a moisturizer, if your doctor allows
Do not skip sessions. Regularity matters
Protect your skin from the sun on treatment days
red_flags: Strong redness, burning, or blisters, like a sunburn
New spots or moles that are changing

faq.q: Is it the same as a tanning bed?
faq.a: No. Here, an exact dose of a specific light is given under a doctor's control. A tanning bed does not replace phototherapy.
Improvement usually shows after a few weeks. With vitiligo it takes longer, sometimes months.

reminders.text: Phototherapy tomorrow. Do not put on creams and do not sunbathe extra.
